$comment: Type-check only (`npm run typecheck` -> tsc -p tsconfig.json). The sources are src/**/*.ts; the shipped lib/ and the root client.js are BUILT artifacts (tsdown) and are committed together with the src that produced them — rebuild with `npm run build` and commit both in the SAME commit (the build-gate forbids shipping src changes without a matching rebuild). Never hand-edit the built output. strict:true is the project-wide baseline; the flags below NARROW it, and none of them is a substitute for a test. exactOptionalPropertyTypes:true is on because this codebase keeps a hard line between "this fact is absent" and "this fact was read and is undefined": an optional property that accepts an explicit `undefined` cannot tell the two apart, and the plugin's own red line is that a value it could not parse must never be rendered as a number (a missing quota limit and a limit of zero must look different). Turning it on cost eight call sites, all of them mechanical (an optional field being handed an `undefined` that the type had declared as absent), and it found one real ambiguity — the `binary.env` row, where the host sent an unset ATOMCODE_BIN as `undefined` while the shared type said "absent, not null". Keep it true; if a signature must accept an explicit undefined, write `?: T | undefined` in THAT signature rather than turning this flag off. The rest of the flags are the ordinary strict set: noUncheckedIndexedAccess (an out-of-range read is `undefined`, not a value), noImplicitOverride / noUnusedLocals / noUnusedParameters / noImplicitReturns / noFallthroughCasesInSwitch (each one is a mistake the compiler can see). Do not widen them for convenience.
